title: Building AI for Creators | Luma & Phota Labs

reader_summary.headline: I think the creativity is building a story.
reader_summary.overview: I think the creativity is building a story. It's not about mastering those tools. It's about directing an agent who can use those tools to achieve your creativity. You can be sort of authentic to that moment, while getting a little bit creative of stuff.

key_points.text: So I just think a lot of developers are having more fun post capturing than before.
key_points.evidence_quote: So I just think a lot of developers are having more fun post capturing than before.

key_points.text: How do you make something unique with the tools you have access to now?
key_points.evidence_quote: How do you make something unique with the tools you have access to now?

key_points.text: There has to be something more than just text.
key_points.evidence_quote: There has to be something more than just text.

key_points.text: If you go to say a studio and you say, make me a 10 second video about a dog jumping in the grass.
key_points.evidence_quote: If you go to say a studio and you say, make me a 10 second video about a dog jumping in the grass, they're never going to take that deal.

thesis: The episode argues that in the age of AI, the most important ingredient in creative work is the person directing the tools rather than the models themselves. It posits that creativity is defined by building a story and composing unique outputs, not by mastering tools or generating content that lacks a human narrative.
